cycles.summary: Authored the source-locked-verification skill to the standard Lawcal legal-tech package: SKILL.md (English), SKILL_HE.md (Hebrew mirror), two references (verification-workflow, claim-types), an offline stdlib-only claim/citation scanner, metadata.json, evidence.json, and this log. The skill's central discipline is anti-fabrication: a citation is never treated as proof of support, and unverifiable sources are graded as such rather than assumed supported. Ran the script self-check (--selftest: OK).

changes.detail: Authored SKILL.md: scope, atomic-claim extraction, citation matching, the Supported/Partial/Unsupported/Unverifiable/Misquoted grading rubric, unsourced-assertion report, anti-fabrication discipline, examples, gotchas, reference links, troubleshooting.
Added SKILL_HE.md: Hebrew RTL mirror of the instructions, examples, gotchas, and reference links.
Added references/verification-workflow.md (end-to-end pass) and references/claim-types.md (what needs a source vs exempt, disguised-fact trap, quotation/quantity rules).
Added metadata.json (author, version 1.0.0, category, bilingual tags + display name/description, supported agents).
Added evidence.json documenting 5 claims sourced to the method references, ABA Model Rule 3.3, FTC substantiation guidance, and the local script self-check.
Verified scripts/claim_scanner.py --selftest passes on python3.11 (stdlib only, no network).

deferrals.reason: Judging whether a cited source actually supports a claim requires reading the source, which is outside a static scanner's ability. The script deliberately stops at first-pass citation detection and defers support grading to the human/agent with source access, per the anti-fabrication rule.
